key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes the perovskite surface potential more uniform and dynamically stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage behavior.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface passivation can directly improve carrier landscape homogeneity in perovskite solar cells, supporting higher and more stable device performance.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measured dark CPD and illuminated SPV.
Compared unpassivated vs AEAPTMS-treated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films.
Separated grain-boundary and grain-interior potential contributions and tracked wavelength-dependent SPV.
evidence_signal: AEAPTMS narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced stabilization time from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results are based on thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translation to full device durability and large-area processing still needs confirmation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
